Subject: Encryption discovery recap and questionnaire kickoff

Hi Emma / Security team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from Oxbridge (please correct if I misstate):
- You process PHI and expect HIPAA controls; BAA required.
- Primary environment is AWS; you currently use AWS KMS for some services and are evaluating customer-managed key (BYOK) patterns and HSM-backed CMKs for new workloads.
- SOC 2 status: you indicated your Type II audit is scheduled but not yet complete.

Open items we need to close to scope a secure demo / design:
1) Desired KMS model: BYOK (customer uploads keys) vs. KMS multi-tenant CMKs vs. HSM-provided keys. Do you have a preference or blocker?
2) Key lifecycle: rotation policy, rotation automation, and retention requirements.
3) Egress / export rules: are there restrictions on where keys may be used or stored?
4) Audit & access: list of people/systems that should have key usage visibility; required audit log retention period.
5) BAA specifics: any clauses that materially affect key custody or logging.

Attachments: I’ve included a vendor security questionnaire (please see the filled copy below when you respond). Also attaching a short SOC2 summary from us to speed mutual evaluation.

Proposed next steps: 
- Emma / Security: please send the filled vendor questionnaire and a short note on your SOC 2 timeline, whether you can provide a SOC 2 report or bridge letter, and any immediate constraints on KMS/HSM approaches (by EOD Friday).
- Redwood (Marcus): review the questionnaire and provide a recommended deployment pattern (BYOK vs Redwood-managed CMK vs HSM-backed) and a one-page risks & mitigations note.
- Schedule: if responses look aligned, we’ll set a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Oxbridge security and Redwood infra the week of 11/23.

Appreciate the collaboration — I’ll track answers here so nothing slips.

Thanks,
Soogin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from our side (high-level):
- SOC 2: We completed Type I earlier this year; Type II audit work is underway with an expected report delivery in early Q1 2027. We can provide interim evidence (control summaries / ISMS documentation) this week.
- KMS/KMS model: Our current baseline uses AWS KMS (KMS-managed CMKs) for most workloads. For workloads handling the most sensitive PHI, we prefer HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM or HSM via KMS) or a BYOK model where we retain key material in our HSM. We are open to options — main constraint is we cannot have key material leaving our control for those PHI workloads.
- Key rotation: We operate on a 12-month rotation baseline but can support shorter rotation windows if necessary; automated rotation preferred.
- Audit logs: We retain KMS/CloudTrail logs for 3 years in a read-only archive; more retention is possible if required.

Attached: completed vendor security questionnaire (filled), and a short key handoff sketch (internal).

Short timeline ask: we can confirm SOC 2 artifact availability by Friday 2026-11-20.

Thanks — happy to jump on a technical call.

Regards,
Emma Jones
Director, Platform Security

Thanks for the ping and sharing the questionnaire — quick read / recommended approach below.

Short answer: Redwood can support the constraint "key material never leaves customer control" but we need to clarify what "never leaves" means operationally and across failure modes. Options: 

Option A — BYOK with HSM key import: Oxbridge keeps a private HSM, exports key material under secure procedures, and imports into a dedicated CMK in the customer-controlled AWS account (or uses a CloudHSM cluster they control). In this model Redwood’s runtime uses the customer-controlled CMK via API calls (we do not store key material). Pros: strong customer control, aligns with PHI requirement. Cons: additional ops for Oxbridge; requires cross-account KMS grants and careful IAM scoping.

Option B — Envelope encryption with customer master key (CMK) in customer account: Redwood generates data keys but they are encrypted (envelope) with a CMK that is in Oxbridge's AWS account and backed by CloudHSM. Data key plaintext never leaves transient memory in Redwood runtime; only the encrypted data key is stored. Pros: good balance; simpler than BYOK import. Cons: requires network connectivity and KMS grants; need to test latency impact.

Option C — Dedicated HSM appliance / on-prem BYOK: for air-gapped or ultra-sensitive workloads, Redwood can integrate with customer HSM via a secure gateway (requires private deployment).

Required clarifying questions / artifacts to request from Oxbridge before the deep-dive: 
- CloudHSM architecture diagram + VPC peering details (if we will reach their HSM over VPC).
- KMS key policy snippets & IAM roles that will be used by Redwood (principals we need).
- Key rotation policy and whether automatic rotation is allowed or must be gated by customer approval.
- Expected QPS (peek token generation) and latency SLOs for calls that require KMS usage — helps profile performance impact.
- Any network egress restrictions or dedicated gateway requirements.

Operational considerations / mitigations: 
- Fallback: define a fallback model if customer KMS is unreachable (can Redwood fall back to a Redwood-managed key with customer approval?). This needs contractual clarity and SLA language.
- Audit trail: ensure CloudTrail + KMS logs are forwarded to Oxbridge read-only S3 bucket or Log Archive; retention configured per their 3-year requirement.
- Performance: if envelope pattern is used, we'll want to batch KMS calls and cache data keys for short windows to prevent token per-request latency.

I’ll draft a 1-page tech note for Oxbridge summarizing the options + recommended configuration and list of artifacts to collect. If we get the CloudHSM diagram and key policy before the call we can be more prescriptive.

—Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
